ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the farming villages of Mehrgarh hold the Kachi Plain of Balochistan (the earliest settlement "dated from 7000 BCE or 5250 BCE").
5500 BCE: the pottery-using Neolithic of Mehrgarh II-VI begins: the Indus page's table puts "Mehrgarh II-VI" (ceramic Neolithic) in the Regionalisation Era "5500-3300".
4000 BCE: the Chalcolithic Togau phase begins at Mehrgarh: "The Togau phase ... c. 4000-3500 BCE".
3500 BCE: Mehrgarh Period IV begins: "Period IV 3500-3250 BCE".

notes: Mehrgarh, the Neolithic and Chalcolithic settlements of the Kachi Plain in Balochistan, treated as a culture. Dates on the page: infobox 'c. 5200 BCE' built and 'c. 2600 BCE' abandoned; 'The earliest settlement is dated from 7000 BCE or 5250 BCE' (Period I aceramic Neolithic 'between 5250 and 4650 BCE' per Mutin and Zazzo, 'pre-7000-5500 BCE' per Jarrige); Togau phase 'c. 4000-3500 BCE'; Period IV '3500-3250 BCE'; Period V '3250-3000 BCE'; the city 'largely abandoned' 'between 2600 BCE and 2000 BCE'. The dossier starts at -6000 (the floor) and ends in 3300, where the Indus Valley Civilization dossier (sa-01) draws its Early Harappan Ravi phase and already includes a 50 km Mehrgarh disc in its 3300 'found' region. The site itself continued to c. 2600 (Periods IV-VII) inside that shape. Extent: the page names the Kachi Plain and gives 'Togau covers around 100 hectares' and a site of '495-acre (2.00 km2)'; a 50 km disc is the placement (the same disc the Indus dossier uses). The Quetta Valley settlements of the late 4th millennium are 'a rise in settlements' on the page, not drawn. 'Hakra Ware' on the page is a Bhirrana (Haryana) matter dated '7380 and 6201 BCE', not Mehrgarh, and is not drawn. Asko Parpola's view that the culture 'migrated into the Indus Valley and became the Indus Valley Civilisation' is set against Jarrige's 'independent origin of Mehrgarh'. The Indus page's chronology table gives 'Early Food Producing Era 7000-5500' (Mehrgarh I) and 'Regionalisation Era' (Mehrgarh II-VI, ceramic Neolithic) from 5500. No Cliopatria shape; the Indus row starts in 3000.
